title: An injective ring map from a domain to a field extends to an embedding of its fraction field
statement: Let $A$ be an integral domain with field of fractions $\operatorname{Frac}(A)$, let $L$ be a field and let $g\colon A\to L$ be an injective ring homomorphism. Then there is a unique ring homomorphism $\tilde g\colon\operatorname{Frac}(A)\to L$ with $\tilde g(a)=g(a)$ for $a\in A$; it is given by $\tilde g(a/s)=g(a)g(s)^{-1}$ for $a,s\in A$, $s\neq0$, and it is injective.
